mappings.note: What music comprises -- singing, playing and dancing together, which is how the interview frames the art. This is the one chapter where the dance-and-craft outcome is literal rather than strained. Rejected LO-105: the answer is a claim about the art form, not a located fact.
Which element gives dance its beauty (lay) -- a technical term of the form. Rejected LO-108: the word belongs to the vocabulary of the art, which this outcome names.
Where Kathak was once confined (temples) -- the history of the dance form. Rejected LO-105: about the art, not about the man.
Which gharana he belongs to -- 'gharana' is a term of the dance lineage. Rejected LO-105: the concept, not a biographical date.
His father's name -- a biographical detail located in the interview. Rejected LO-107: nothing about the art form is tested.
From when he dates Kathak's beginnings (the Mahabharata and Ramayana) -- the form's antiquity. Rejected LO-105: a claim about the tradition.
Which bond he calls sacred between guru and pupil (the ganda) -- a term belonging to the practice of the art. Rejected LO-108: the word is the art's, not general vocabulary.
Where the Lucknow gharana's people came from (Hariya village) -- a located fact. Rejected LO-107: geography, not the art.
In which of the three body, meditation and austerity are practised (dance) -- his claim about what dancing is. Rejected LO-105: a proposition about the art.

Which gharana he belongs to -- the lineage term again. Rejected LO-105 as before. NOTE: this item duplicates an earlier one in the chapter, and its options carry OCR noise ('jaipuran', 'banaras gharaanna').
What his father did (dancer) -- biographical detail. Rejected LO-107: about the man.
From whom he learnt to dance (all of them) -- biographical. Rejected LO-107: who taught him, not what the art is.
What else interested him besides Kathak -- located list. Rejected LO-107: his other pursuits, not the dance.
What he changed in Kathak performance (the way of telling the story) -- a change to the art itself. Rejected LO-105: about the form, not the man.
What matters in Kathak, per him (lay) -- a technical judgement about the form. Rejected LO-102: it names an element, not an argued idea.
When his training with his father began (childhood) -- biographical. Rejected LO-107: a date, not the art.
Who helped most through the money troubles (his mother) -- biographical. Rejected LO-100: the item asks who, not about women's position.
What dance comprises, per him -- body, meditation, austerity: his account of the art. Rejected LO-105: a claim about dance.
How dancers stand to the taal when the tabla plays -- the technical arrangement of the performance. Rejected LO-105: a matter of practice, not biography.
Whose styles he took into his art (father's and uncles') -- the transmission of style within the form. Rejected LO-105: about style, not about a fact of his life.
What was kept of the old tradition (the core elements of the dance). Rejected LO-105: about the form.
What he taught his daughters (dance) -- the bare fact. Rejected LO-100, which I keep for the items that put the question of girls' education and skill.

What he holds necessary for women -- education or a skill. Gender is named in this outcome among the sensitive issues on which a learner should form a reasoned view, so this is a real fit rather than a fallback. Rejected LO-102: the subject is women's position, not his art.
Blank is 'komalta', said of Odissi and Manipuri -- comparing the qualities of dance styles. Rejected LO-108: the term is used of the art form.
Blank is 'Kathak' in the claim about the tradition's age. Rejected LO-105: about the form.
Blank is 'nritya' in the sentence about earnings from programmes -- a fact of his household. Rejected LO-107: the sentence is about money, not the art.
Blank is 'ladkiyon' in the claim that girls must have some education or skill -- the gender question again. Rejected LO-105: the sentence's whole point is the social claim.
Blank is 'sangeet', joining singing, playing and dancing. Rejected LO-105: about the art.
Blank is 'tabla', the instrument he beat from infancy -- an instrument of the form. Rejected LO-105: the instrument is the point.
Blank is 'shaastriya sangeet' in the comparison of his life to its colours -- the simile borrows the vocabulary of classical music. Rejected LO-108, which covers the learner's own use of words.
Blank is 'saamoohik', the defining mark of folk dance. Rejected LO-106: the item asks the word, not appreciation of folk material.
What being each other's helper inspires -- his idea, which the learner must grasp. Rejected LO-105: no line states it as a fact.

WHY girls must have education or a skill -- keyed to self-reliance, so the learner must follow a reasoned position on women's independence. Rejected LO-102: the subject is the social issue, which this outcome names.
What serves one in need, per him (a skill) -- his proposition. Rejected LO-100: stated of anyone, not specifically of women.
Which highest honour he held (Padma Vibhushan) -- biographical. Rejected LO-107: an award, not the art.
Whose example gave him the taste for painting -- biographical. Rejected LO-107: painting is not the dance.
When he sat down to paint (after midnight) -- biographical. Rejected LO-107 as above.
What he might have been but a dancer (an engineer) -- biographical. Rejected LO-102: a passing remark, not a proposition.
From when he beat the tabla -- biographical. Rejected LO-107, used where the instrument itself is the answer.
What he looked for before tying the ganda (true dedication) -- his handling of a custom of the art. Rejected LO-105: about the practice of teaching, not about his life.
